text:
maria: Heads up — the latency dashboard for endpoint rollups looks off after we started routing by model-tag. p50 barely moved but p95/p99 jumped by ~400ms for several endpoints.

chetan: can you paste the query you're using? thinking maybe the rollup is averaging then computing percentiles.

maria: here's the metric query I used (promql):

```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, endpoint))
```

We group by endpoint path but our router mashes model param into endpoint label for some requests so paths are duplicated.

alex: histogram_quantile on summed buckets is OK if buckets align, but if endpoints have different bucket sets or we mix streaming / non-streaming, it can lie.

maria: Right — I think the router is sending a small subset of high-latency backend traffic into the same 'endpoint' label because we canonicalize paths after the fact. So the rollup over heterogeneous distributions produces an inflated tail.

samir: short-term fix: exclude streaming routes from rollup. Long-term: store t-digests or exemplars per endpoint and merge them. Chetan, we have t-digest proto implemented for traces right?

chetan: yes, we have a t-digest proto in eng-metrics repo. We didn't enable rollup merge though. Enabling would increase storage but make percentiles correct across shards.

alex: :thumbsup: cost question — how much storage & CPU would digest-merge add? ballpark?

chetan: rough estimate: ~10-15% storage increase for digest blobs, CPU ~5% on ingest nodes. I'd rather run a canary for a day.

observability-bot: alert: dashboard-percentile-surge on /generate completed route — rule triggered at 1748001300

maria: samir can you run a canary comparing current histogram_quantile vs merged t-digest for the last 2 hours? I'll prepare a query and synthetic load.

samir: on it. will run load with 10% streaming traffic mixed. posting results in ~20m.

jessica: also let's add a note in the console UI explaining that p99 may be misleading across mixed route groups. quick UX fix.

maria: good call. I'll draft a small tooltip: 'Percentiles are computed over the aggregated label set. For mixed traffic (streaming vs unary) prefer per-route breakdowns or merged t-digests.'

alex: thanks — and we should add a lint to router canonicalization to prevent accidental label collapse.
